title: 3Sum
statement:
Given an integer array `nums`, return all the triplets `[nums[i], nums[j], nums[k]]` such that `i != j`, `i != k`, `j != k`, and `nums[i] + nums[j] + nums[k] == 0`.

The solution set must not contain duplicate triplets.

checkpoints.question: The total is still negative and l has caught up to r. What happens next?
options: Stop this pass — there's no room left between the markers — and move to the next fixed number
checkpoints.answer: Stop this pass — there's no room left between the markers — and move to the next fixed number
checkpoints.why: Once the markers meet, there are no more pairs left to try for this fixed number, so the sweep moves on to the next one.

checkpoints.question: The total is exactly zero. What should happen to the markers?
options: Stop entirely — this is the only triple
Record the triple, then move both markers inward to keep looking
checkpoints.answer: Record the triple, then move both markers inward to keep looking
checkpoints.why: One zero-sum triple doesn't rule out others. Recording it and continuing to sweep inward can turn up more.

checkpoints.question: The next fixed number, nums[2], equals nums[1] (both -1). What should happen when the sweep reaches it?
options: Process it normally — it might find a new triple
Skip it — any triple it starts would duplicate one already found
checkpoints.answer: Skip it — any triple it starts would duplicate one already found
checkpoints.why: Fixing the same value twice in a row explores the same territory nums[1] already covered, producing duplicate triples.

hints: Sorting first turns "find three numbers that cancel out" into something a two-pointer sweep can handle one fixed number at a time.

With the array sorted and one number fixed, the remaining two behave exactly like the two-sum-on-a-sorted-array pattern: a pair too small only gets bigger by moving the left marker in, a pair too big only gets smaller by moving the right marker in.

Sort the array. Fix one index as the first number of the triple and sweep it left to right; at each fixed number, sweep a left marker and a right marker inward from the remaining stretch, comparing the three-number total to zero and moving one marker at a time. Skip a fixed number that repeats the previous one, and skip repeats of the inner markers too, so no triple is produced twice.
